## MY WRONG CLAIM, corrected by measurement (keep this lesson in front of the wave)
- I recorded: 'item 2 must update 5 guard tests in the same commit or they go red', because those paths appear in those
  files. Grepping what the tests actually ASSERT disproves it: NO test asserts which TSX file imports which CSS.
  cartExtraction.test.ts reads the 6 sheets from SALES_DIR and concatenates classNames from TSX_FILE + ADDITIONAL_TSX_FILES,
  asserting (1) every className used has a rule :88, (2) no className in >1 file :101, (3) every className defined in CSS
  is REACHABLE from those files :116 ('no dead classes'). The compliance tests read CSS directly.
- The REAL rule, which is narrower and per-extraction: any markup moved OUT of PosScreen.tsx into a file not listed in
  ADDITIONAL_TSX_FILES makes its classNames unreachable -> :116 fails. So each extraction must add its new component to
  that list in the same commit. Moving an `import './X.css'` line by itself breaks nothing while the .css files stay put.
- This is the same failure as last wave's 'nobody imports it': I had a real grep hit list and read a conclusion into it
  that the file does not support. A path appearing in a test is not a statement being asserted. Measure the assertion.

## ca5d58957 fix(sales): render quick tender amounts through formatMoney with no float math
- 2 files (+50/-11): PaymentModal.tsx AND PaymentModal.test.tsx in ONE commit, deliberately atomic - a behaviour change and
  the assertion that pins it must never land apart, or the tree has a red commit in its history. Gate on the merged tree
  before committing: 92 passed / 92, typecheck 0, eslint 0, and `10 ** exp` + `id-ID` occurrence counts now 0 in the file.
- The updated assertion is `/^\$ 10[.,]000[.,]00$/` with a comment: pinned by PROPERTY (symbol not ISO code; exp-honoured
  decimals) over either separator, so it survives id OR en and still FAILS if someone reintroduces the code+no-decimals
  hybrid. The worker's reason for not deriving via formatMoney in the test is sound and better than my suggestion: the
  harness has no locale provider, so a derived expectation would hardcode 'id' and agree with itself while disagreeing with

- FINDING 1 (E2E/a11y hazard, reported): the shift button's ACCESSIBLE NAME is pos-shift-open-aria = 'Open a new shift',
  while its visible text is pos-shift-open-btn = 'Open'. Its first draft asserted the visible label and failed. Any doc or
  Playwright spec that quotes visible text as the name is targeting the wrong string.
- FINDING 2 (systemic, worth the user's attention): requiredLocalized() does NOT throw when a key is absent - it returns the
  raw key id plus a DEV console.warn. Demonstrated by the fact that tables-title / kds-title / settings-page-title /
  retail-fn-history / retail-fn-stok are not in shared.ftl at all (they live in tables.ftl / kds.ftl / settings.ftl /
  sales.ftl), yet a test bundling only sales+shared still passes. A missing chrome key therefore renders a button literally
  labelled 'kds-title' in production with nothing going red. The commit-time bundle-parity gate (step 2, eight surfaces)
  and CI's full-tree scan) is what should catch a genuinely missing key - I have NOT verified that this specific accessor is
  one of the eight surfaces, so I state the risk, not a guarantee. The runtime is certainly silent.
- Its process notes on its own drafts (two baseDefaults fields had to be vi.fn() spies not noop; case 4 needed explicit
  unmount() because a 77-prop panel can be mounted several times and getByRole('region') is document-wide) are the kind of
  detail that saves the next writer an iteration, so they are in the file, not just the report.

## FEATURE-GATE DECISION: NOT IMPLEMENTED — measured, and the measurement prevented an outage
- I proposed this fix this morning and listed it as the #1 next action. It is now REJECTED on evidence, and I am recording
  the rejection rather than the intention, because the next reader would otherwise try it.
- Decisive chain: `feature:` filters NAV ONLY (menu-registry/index.ts:99-102 -> AppLayout.tsx:92 / TabletAppLayout.tsx:55);
  the render path uses getPage (AppShell.tsx:471) + isPageAccessible (:473) which read role/permission and never .feature;
  AND isEnabled is default-DENY (useFeatures.ts:130-133, empty Set :96); AND a fresh install has an EMPTY feature registry
  (no migration seeds feature rows; features.rs:516-520; settings_tests.rs:77-81 asserts count()==0); AND the dev-mock
  returns names that are not real feature keys (dev-mock/handlers/system.ts:456). Adding the gate = blanking the POS for
  fresh/offline/dev-mock tenants. store-pos is allowed on FREE (workspaces_tests.rs:325) and
  list_all_workspaces_scoped has no entitlement filter (oz-bridge/workspaces.rs:693-719) - so the 'asymmetry' state is

# RENAMING IS NOT COSMETIC HERE: `todo-` IS A MACHINE TOKEN
- .agents/skills/docs-auditor/scripts/check-dead-refs.py:200 grants a plan doc its HISTORICAL dead-ref exemption iff
  name.startswith(('todo-','plan-','prd-')). Putting `done-` in FRONT voids the exemption, so a FINISHED plan is
  reclassified as a live document and starts generating findings about itself.
- Measured invoice, already paid by the other session's 37 moves: the checker exits 1 with 33 unresolved refs in 10 live
  docs, of which 6 are `done-todo-*` files carrying 28 of the 33. (5 findings pre-date the moves: AGENTS.md x2,
  docs/operations/runbook.md, a manager journal - do not blame all 33 on them.)
- Deeper: a plan filename is a PROVENANCE MARKER across code, not just prose. After those moves, 50 files still cite
  `todo-global-saas-2.md` and 11 cite `todo-kds-agents-1.md`, including
  crates/oz-core/migrations/20261005_kds_routing_rules.sql:1, crates/oz-core/src/migrations.rs:311,
  scripts/ipc-parity-allowlist.json:2, scripts/generate-pg-migration.py:96, screenExtraction.test.ts:270, kds.ftl +
  kds.id.ftl, and a website pricing test. `todo-tools.md` alone is cited in 17 lines across 10 files - including BOTH
  Fluent bundles (shared.ftl:571, shared.id.ftl:563). Two files created TODAY (handlers/staff.ts:6,
  handlers/workspaces.ts:8) name their plan in shipped production headers.
- Nothing fails MECHANICALLY on a rename: 0 hits for todo- in AGENTS.md/README/gates.json/.githooks, and NO test reads a
  plan by path. The cost is entirely citation integrity - which is exactly the class of damage that looks free at commit
  time and is permanent later.
- DECIDED VOCABULARY (5a77d17d, Option B executed as C): two names on ONE axis. `done-todo-` means the file's own
  acceptance command RAN AND PASSED. Parked / superseded / audit are *reasons acceptance is absent* and belong in a dated
  header line, not the filename. A plan whose check:all never ran stays `todo-` however complete its code - which makes a
  false 'done' UNNAMEABLE rather than merely discouraged. Five-value prefix ladders were rejected: they mint a checker
  vocabulary change and strand 2-7 dated citations each.
- SUPERSEDED != DONE, argued: obligations were TRANSFERRED, not discharged. kds-agents-1/-2 still show 8 open boxes each
  on disk, and the merged doc carries a 16-in/16-out reconciliation at :125 plus an explicit open box preserving
  todo-kds.md's sequencing constraint 'so the unblock is a recorded decision, not a silent overwrite'.
  So a `done-` rename there would assert a falsehood in a file whose open boxes are still visible. And it would break 2 of
  the 12 real markdown sibling links (](./todo-...) ) — the only breaking kind.
- FUNDED: (a) 1fb707c5 -> widen the :200 exemption to substring so `done-todo-` is safe to ever use, with before/after
  counts and a proof the checker still catches a real broken ref (a checker that reports nothing is disabled, not fixed);
  (b) 79c2aada -> the naming invariant into BOTH AGENTS.md mirrors, with verify-agents-mirrors.py + verify-ci-docs-drift.py
  required to stay green and instructions to REVERT if either reddens.

# ACCEPTANCE GATE DECISION (10:14) — what `npm run check:all` actually is, and what I will NOT do with it
- check:all = `node ../scripts/check-ui.mjs`, eight legs: 1 ESLint 2 TypeScript typecheck 3 Unit tests (vitest, 600 s)
  4 i18n lint 5 FTL dedupe 6 Bundle budget (npm run bundle:check, 300 s) 7 E2E (Playwright PROVISIONED, 900 s, gated on
  `dockerAvailable()` = `docker info` with a 10 s timeout) 8 Perf smoke (600 s, gated on playwrightAvailable()).
- Docker IS up here (server 29.4.3), so leg 7 WOULD run: compose-provision cloud+license+redis, start Vite on :1420,
  Playwright, then tear down. That is cross-session blast radius on a shared daemon and shared ports — a concurrent
  session running `cargo tauri dev` or the shared `oz-pg-test-15432` container would be disturbed by my teardown, and I
  would not see it happen. DECISION: do not run legs 7-8 unattended.
- THE TRAP I AVOIDED BY READING THE SOURCE: AGENTS.md says the stale-image guard is 'Skipped under CI', and I first read
  that as 'E2E is skipped under CI'. It is not. `scripts/run-e2e.mjs:282` is inside `assertImagesFresh()` — setting
  CI=true makes the runner TRUST whatever images are on disk ('CI detected - trusting the images built by the workflow')
  and RUN E2E ANYWAY against them. So `CI=true npm run check:all` would not save time; it would silently produce WEAKER
  evidence while looking like a full green gate. Rule: a doc's summary of a guard is not the guard - read the function.
- PLAN: on a quiet tree run legs 1-6 as six explicit commands and record exit + counts per leg. Legs 7-8 recorded as NOT
  RUN, with the reason. Consequence, stated up front: NO plan gets a `done-` rename from me on the strength of check:all
  today. The boxes instead get an accurate sentence about which legs ran, so a later reader is not told a suite passed
  that never executed. PARKED for the user: one deliberate E2E+perf run (with `--build` so the freshness guard is real),
  scheduled when no other session is using the daemon, which is the only thing that makes those boxes close honestly.
- Mirror pair verified: §4 'Plan-doc naming is a checker token' present in BOTH (AGENTS.md, .agents/AGENTS.md), and the
  deliberate dead-ref annotation is in both at AGENTS.md:246 / .agents:173 - wording preserves the incident narrative and
  records that the script was added by 9deab2c16 and deleted by e3aff7b56, so there is no successor path to repoint at.

  cannot grant a manager anything. The backend already logs the hazard itself: `crates/oz-bridge/src/data.rs:291-296`
  emits event `backup_ungated_no_session` with `skipped_permission = DATA_EXPORT`, and the doc comment at :286-289 states
  the design intent is visibility, not closure ('a bypass that cannot be closed quietly is at least visible').
WHAT IT COSTS: pre-login backup dies. `sessionToken` is `rawSessionToken ?? ''` (:165) and WorkspaceContext mints it only
  when an instance+user resolve, so a single-user offline install that has not logged in - or whose login is BROKEN - can
  still make a backup today and could not afterwards. `.agents/review-backlog-codebase-review.md:89` documents the brick
  scenario: the only in-app restore is .ozpkg row import via THIS screen, strictly after migrations, and export/import
  ALREADY require a token. So the asymmetry is real: backup-without-login is currently the one thing that works when
  login is broken.
IS THE HAZARD LOAD-BEARING? For behaviour, no. For RECORDS, yes - three suites pin it deliberately:
  `DataManagementBackup.test.tsx:286` describe = 'Backup with NO session token (known hazard, not a goal)' and its :279
  instruction is 'IF BACKUP GATING LANDS, INVERT THIS TEST, DO NOT DELETE IT'; `data_tests.rs:45` BACKUP_EVENT asserts the
  event fires per ungated call and `:796` asserts the scoped path does NOT emit it; `testing.rs:226` records that the
  event-capture assertion 'was a silent pass without it' - the harness was fixed FOR this pin. Nothing in ui/e2e touches
  backup (0 hits). The two Rust event tests survive a UI-side change because the commands stay registered
  (`apps/desktop-client/src/lib.rs:894-897`); only the UI test needs inverting, and it tells me to invert it, not delete it.
MY RECOMMENDATION: DO IT, on the UI side only, inverting the pinned test as its own comment instructs, and keep the backend
  commands registered (deregistering is the WIDER change that would strand a bricked install). Pair it with the
  BackupSection extraction so the ternaries move and change in one reviewable place. NOT executed unattended because it
  removes a recovery capability from offline installs - that is a product posture call, and a worker deciding it at 3 a.m.
  is exactly what I am here to prevent.
ALSO NOTED: this is the ONLY plan family where nothing is stale-ticked - 0 of 11 boxes are done-on-disk, and two boxes
  (:111 AuditRetention UI, :130 FactoryResetConfirmationModal) ask for capabilities that were never built (`git grep -i
  'factory_reset'` over ui/src, crates, apps -> 0 hits). So it is a real unstarted lane, not a bookkeeping mirage.

# get_setting: VERDICT FIX, and the reason it is low-priority is the same fact
- Live consumer exists: `ui/src/frontend/shell/UpdateBanner.tsx:144` -> getSetting() -> api/settings.ts:213 -> command
  `get_setting`. Production returns NULL for an unset key (`platform/core/src/settings/raw.rs:32` `None => Ok(None)`,
  surfaced as Result<Option<String>> in both shells' commands/settings.rs, and ALREADY PINNED IN RUST by
  `crates/oz-bridge/src/settings_tests.rs:336` get_setting_returns_none_for_missing_key). The mock returns '' for every
  key, so the mock cannot express a distinction production makes and tests.
- Why low-priority, measured rather than assumed: every consumer predicate (`prev &&`, `if (raw)`, === 'true',
  !== 'false', parseInt(x ?? '')) maps '' and null to the SAME verdict today. So it is a latent lie, not a live bug.
- CHARACTERIZATION TEST SHIPPED, green, asserting the bug is PRESENT (expect(value).toBe('')), 4 cases, 706 ms - it goes
  red when someone fixes the mock and is meant to be deleted with the fix. That is the right instrument.
- THE COLLISION, and it is the finding I would have missed: `dev-mock-scoped-aliases.test.ts:81` asserts
  `expect(value).not.toBeNull()` for `get_setting_scoped`. So the honest fix (`() => null`, plus actually registering
  `get_setting_scoped`, which is registered nowhere today) BREAKS A CURRENTLY-GREEN TEST. Whoever fixes this must resolve
  that collision ON PURPOSE rather than 'fixing' whichever test is red. Recorded before any fix lands.

# useCartTax aliasing FIXED (committed) - and the worker disproved MY 'behavioural non-event' framing with an A/B probe
- I wrote 'call out that it is a behavioural NON-EVENT'. FALSE, measured against a HEAD copy: the shared reference let
  React's Object.is BAIL-OUT skip a re-render, so the old code rendered 1x and the new renders 2x on the null-token mount
  and on failure-with-no-cache. Values read by the screens are identical; the render COUNT is not. A non-event claim would
  have shipped a real, if small, behaviour change unnoticed - which is the exact class of thing I have been deleting all day.
- DECISION I OWN (its offer): do NOT take the one-line `setState(prev => prev.severity === 'unknown' ? prev :
  createUnknownState())` that restores render parity. Reason: it makes the hook re-derive its own severity at every write,
  inventing semantics to recover a render that only happens on an unknown-classifying transition (no session token, or a
  failed fetch with no cache). Correctness over a micro-render, and 105 screen cases passed with the extra render. If a
  profile ever shows the bail-out mattering, that one-liner is recorded here and in the code comment at :151.
- Its strongest proof form, worth copying into briefs: the two new tests observe the HOOK'S OWN returned objects and name no
  factory, so the SAME assertion text ran red before and green after with no edit between runs - nothing in the assertion
  tracks the fix. Ask for that shape whenever a fix is a rename-or-extract, where a factory-named test can go green by
  accident.
- It also corrected me twice more: the 'never mutated' comment does not exist in this file (the assumption was implicit, i.e.
  nothing warned the next reader), and my 'CartTaxWatcher 10 cases' was 8. It deleted UNKNOWN_STATE outright rather than
  documenting the footgun - no readers left - while IDLE_TAX_STATE stays exported because three test files import it. That
  asymmetry was reasoned, not defaulted.
- No stray file from my bad path: it globbed first, ls-files --others on features/sales/hooks is 0. The bad-path risk I
  raised did not materialise.

# TOP RENAME-EARNING CANDIDATE AT THE GATE (this is the user's actual instruction, so it gets priority, not a nice-to-have)
The objective says rename a todo when it is DONE. AGENTS.md 4 says that means its OWN acceptance command was RUN and PASSED.
So the way to earn a rename is not to finish code - it is to find a plan whose remaining open boxes ARE acceptance runs and
run them. Candidates by box count, re-measured by fence-aware awk: devmock-agents-3 (4 open / 10 ticked - :140 was recorded
as 'the acceptance run'), tools-agents-3 (3 open, gate met but `check:all` never run), pos-screen-agents-2 (3 open),
cloud-sync-1 (5 open but three of them are the PG-backed run I cannot honestly tick while oz-pg-test-15432 is Exited),
font-system (5 open).
PLAN AT THE QUIET TREE: after legs 1-6 pass, for each candidate run ITS OWN cited command verbatim (the string in the file,
not my paraphrase - that rule exists because I got a SHA wrong from memory today), then:
 - if every open box in the file is met by a run that passed, tick with the dated evidence and RENAME the file IN PLACE with
   the `done-` prefix (git mv, one pathspec commit, root location preserved per AGENTS.md 4 - NOT into .agents/archived/);
 - if any box remains unmet or unrunnable (PG container, E2E, --release runner), write a dated line naming which, and leave
   the name alone. Half-done is not done, and a false rename costs more than a tenth day of `todo-`.
NOTE the asymmetry I must not paper over in the report: zero renames today is NOT because nothing finished - ~930 lines left
six hot files and two latent defects were closed with mutation proofs - it is because acceptance was never RUN on a quiet
tree while several lanes were mid-flight, which is a sequencing choice I made deliberately and can reverse at the gate.
# I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE DEFECT I HAD BEEN FUNDING (and the finding is better than the fix)
- I called the 12 DATA_TYPES strings 'hardcoded English needing translation'. They were NOT: all 12 keys existed in
  settings.ftl:583-594 AND settings.id.ftl:487-498, fully reviewed, real Indonesian ('Produk', 'Kategori', 'Penjualan'...).
  The defect was WIRING - the table carried raw English while its own keys sat UNREFERENCED, i.e. verify-ftl-orphans' idea of
  debt, and '0 hits for data-mgmt-type-' at HEAD proves they were orphans before this pass. Zero Indonesian invented because
  none was needed. My brief asked it not to guess translations; the right question was 'are the keys there already'.
- WHY the raw English was ever there, per the lane: the model's shape genuinely fights Fluent, four ways:
  (1) <Localized> needs a STATIC JSX child as the fallback, so a .map() over a table structurally cannot use it and must
     fall back to getString/requiredLocalized, which has no fallback slot at all.
  (2) The DRY form (`data-mgmt-type-${key}` at the call site) is INVISIBLE to the parity gate - it printed exactly that
     class of miss. So a message table must store LITERAL ids as fields, i.e. be deliberately less DRY than a data table
     wants to be. New rule, journal-only until someone writes it in a doc: in a Fluent-policed repo, tables store literal keys.
  (3) requiredLocalized fails SOFT: missing key logs a DEV warning and returns the ID string (:37-42), so a typo renders
     'data-mgmt-type-produts' to a cashier with no red anywhere. That makes (2) load-bearing, not stylistic.
  (4) The same six names live in THREE places: both bundles, the model, and dynamicFluentFamilies.test.ts:62-69 - which also
     omits the six -desc twins and still cites the old file. Follow-up dispatched to make it import DATA_TYPES instead.
- KDS chips committed (guard released, 187 verified green by me): KdsScreen 979, KdsZoneChips 91 ln. Honest net -21 vs my
  ~31; plan forecast 2 props, actual 5 (it missed the keyboard handler and the chip ref array, both stayed in the screen).
  NOTE: the plan's KdsHeaderToolbar.tsx does not exist and was never cut - the chips name is the lane's, and the plan's own
  slice-3 box stays legitimately OPEN.
# TWO GATE-SEMANTICS RULES, both from a worker retracting its OWN published command (this is the best kind of finding)
1. `verify-bundle-parity.py --staged-only` EXITS 0 WHEN IT VERIFIED NOTHING. Run with the wrong path base it printed:
   'received 3 path(s) but none are eligible ... nothing to verify. Returning 0 informational.' -> exit 0, zero coverage.
   RULE: `0 missing key(s)` is evidence ONLY when the same output says `scanned N file(s)` with N > 0. Run it from the repo
   ROOT with `ui/`-prefixed paths. My headline conclusion stood (that run printed bundle totals) but the COMMAND I published
   could not fail - and I am keeping the retraction, not the headline.
2. `--include-key-fields` reads ONE id per object literal: it saw 6 of the model's 12 literals (all labelIds, zero
   descriptionIds) even though both sit on the same lines. So HALF the table has never had a static gate, and
   `requiredLocalized(l10n, dt.descriptionId)` passes a VARIABLE, which is also uncheckable. The only thing ever verifying
   those six keys was dynamicFluentFamilies.test.ts - which until today did not enumerate them. That is the argument for a
   wiring test over a tool change, and it retires my assumption that 'the parity gate covers the model'.
# DESIGN TENSION BEHIND ALL SEVEN RESTATES (this is the answer to the question I keep asking about Fluent vs data)
A family can only be wiring-checked if its domain exists as a runtime `const` array. Five of the seven restated families live
in TS `type`s (NodeType, quadrant unions, status unions) or across languages (Rust/DB), so they are INVISIBLE at runtime and
cannot be imported by a test - hence the pattern of parallel lists. Cheapest real fix is where a const already exists
(inv-log: `INVENTORY_TRANSACTION_TYPE_KEYS` - dispatched; and the sales view-modes case, one-line export away). Everywhere
else, turning a restate into a wiring check is a production change first, and I am not funding those as drive-bys.
- Copies measured: inventory log types x3, topology new-node x4 (incl. topologySemantics.json), menu quadrants x4 (incl.
  reports.ftl). None fixed beyond data-mgmt, per fence.
- The lane also corrected its own file header (claimed 2 imported families, 4 already were) and noted the stale comment
  pointing at DataManagementScreen.tsx is now fixed to the model path with the 'a miss prints the id to a cashier' warning.
# PARKED ITEM ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, and it turned out to be a BUG not a ruling
- Topology-write among built-ins: Admin (rbac_presets.rs:253) + Owner via `["*"]` at :46. Manager/Staff/Auditor/Custom do
  NOT carry it, and topology_command_tests.rs:1399-1415 ASSERTS a manager must be denied. Six presets, six roles; there is
  no cashier/floor/kitchen preset at all - rbac.rs:281 says the retired cashier/kitchen roles fold into Staff (migration 129).
- No KDS-style role-vs-key inversion at shell<->kernel: presets store permission KEYS, commands check KEYS, and the UI helper
  hasGrantedPermission honours `*` and `domain:*`. The break is one hand-picked PROXY on the client:
  `TopologyScreen.tsx:114-119` gates can-save on `staff:update` (Manager HAS it) instead of `topology:write` (Manager LACKS
  it), with a comment saying it avoids 'a flaky IPC round-trip' - i.e. it bypasses `can_save_topology`, a probe that already
  exists and is registered (desktop lib.rs:1205). Result: manager -> /settings route gate passes -> deep link -> editor
  loads -> Save renders ENABLED -> PermissionDenied on click. SettingsDeepLink.test.tsx:201-243 proves the arrival path.
- DISPATCHED as a fix (TopologyScreen.tsx + its test), with the trap named in advance: a raw `perms.includes('topology:write')`
  would LOCK OWNER OUT because Owner grants `*` - the wildcard helper is mandatory, not optional.

  take zero props, so the page's Save bar and the cards' save paths are TWO DISJOINT WRITE CHANNELS - a draft reducer would

# SETTINGS DIRTY-FLAG VERDICT: DEAD-FEATURE, but the CAUSE was wrong in my brief and the fix must wait for the right reason
- My brief framed it as 'nobody calls setIsDirty(true)'. The measurement says the real cause: four `sections/*` components
  DECLARE `markDirty: () => void` and CALL it at ~15 sites (AppearanceSection :56,68,89,101,122,150,152; GeneralSection
  :77,100,124,147,187; ReceiptSection :47,68) - but `renderSection` (SettingsPage.tsx:461-489, 14 case arms) instantiates
  only `screens/*`, and the sections are imported by __tests__ + two GUARD LISTS (screenExtraction:315-319,
  nativeTooltipCompliance:190) and nothing in features/. So the dirty path was never unwired; its entire half of the page
  was replaced by the flat-IA cards and the page kept the gauges. 'A feature that was never removed, only unmounted.'
- Confirmed dead reads: dirty dot permanently -hidden (:586), Revert permanently -hidden (:592) AND tabIndex -1 (:595) while
  still in the DOM with a live onClick, guard can never prompt (useUnsavedChangesGuard :58/:75 early-return on dirtyRef),
  syncApiKey permanently '' (setSyncApiKey has ONLY test writers) so the save hook's :168/:196-199 true branches are dead, and
  SettingsPage.tsx:144 is `const [, setSyncApiKeyVisible]` - a DISCARDED setter, i.e. the key UI was removed on purpose.
- The repo KNOWS: SettingsPage.test.tsx:12-13 header says 'nothing on the page can become dirty' and :570 pins 'does not
  block window close while nothing is dirty'. useUnsavedChangesGuard.test.tsx covers the hook by passing a `dirty` PROP,
  never through the page. And the dead classes are grandfathered in screenExtraction externalClasses:359-360.
- So: NOT a data-loss bug on ordinary navigation, because every live surface (screens/*, workspace-cards/*) persists itself.
  The LIVE version of this machinery elsewhere is DERIVED, not stateful: NodeTopologyEditor.tsx:666 useMemo + :683
  onDirtyChange + applyPanel:370. That is the pattern; SettingsPage's copy is vestigial. useUnsavedChangesGuard must stay -
  topology is its real consumer.
- DELETION IS NOT FUNDED YET, two reasons: (1) SettingsPage.tsx is a live lane's file right now, (2) the sharper question is
  open - if page Save replays mount-time values over newer card-owned scoped writes, then deleting the gauges hides a stale-
  write hazard instead of removing dead chrome, and the three candidate fixes (wire the flag / delete the page save /
  rehydrate on markSettingsUpdated) are three different products. Measurement dispatched. Also: retiring sections/* forces

# SEVERITY CHANGE: the stale-write hazard is LIVE TODAY, no migration required, and it deletes a configured value
- Chain, all measured: a PARTIAL load (`hasPartialError`, toast at SettingsPage:282) leaves `syncServerUrl === ''` -> the
  fan-out sends `serverUrl: syncApiKey?...` no: `serverUrl: syncServerUrl || null` (useSettingsSave.ts:167) -> the server does
  `args.server_url.as_deref().unwrap_or("")` and `set_sync_server_url(url)` UNCONDITIONALLY (sync.rs:64-82), so null CLEARS the
  row. A user who opens Settings during a degraded load and presses Ctrl+S **wipes a configured sync URL**. Both branches are
  already pinned in Rust (`update_sync_settings_deserialize_no_key`, `update_sync_settings_data_clear_url_writes_empty_row`),
  i.e. the server behaves exactly as designed; the client is the defect.
- The link the researcher flagged as unverified is now CLOSED and benign: `apiKey` uses `if let Some(..)` -> absent PRESERVES.
  So the scary-sounding field is safe and the quiet one is not. My brief asked it not to assume the benign answer; it measured.
- Also measured: the page renders ZERO editable fields (one <input>, the search box, :553; 0 of the 11 receipt / 5 store /
  sync / brand fields), so under a correct diff today's Save is ALWAYS a no-op. Two initializer bugs sit next to it:
  `useState<ReceiptSettingsDto>` (:107-118) omits `taxRoundingMode` (Rust has a serde default -> silently rewritten) and
  `useState<StoreSettingsDto>` (:120-126) omits `logo`, which in Rust is a NON-Option String with NO default
  (settings.rs:177) against `logo?: string` in the UI type -> a pre-hydrate save can hard-fail deserialization.
- Contract-change consequences it derived from the code: a skipped task vanishes from `saveTasks`, so
  `saveResult(name)` returns FALSE for skipped (skipped encoded as failed), and the success gate `failed < saveTasks.length`
  reads `0 < 0` = false when everything is skipped -> **the button silently does nothing, no toast**, and 1-of-1 failure is
  indistinguishable from all-skipped. Hence: three-way {fulfilled|rejected|skipped}, an explicit skipped set, a zero-task
  short-circuit BEFORE setSaving(true), per-task snapshot refresh (today the refresh is inside the success branch, so a
  PARTIAL failure still commits every draft value as saved -> dirty clears and Revert targets values the server never got),
  and `savedSnapshotRef === null` must mean 'write nothing', not 'write everything', because there is exactly one reachable
  pre-hydrate render where the save bar exists.
- Coverage truth: `useSettingsSave` has NO dedicated test file; its entire coverage is SettingsPage.test.tsx. The 31
  SettingsContext cases are unaffected BY CONSTRUCTION (that file mounts neither page nor hook) - my tripwire survives.
  Three page cases go red and must be REWRITTEN to edit a field first (:432, :446, :498): that is a behaviour reversal, not
  a move, and I am recording it as such rather than letting it look like incidental test churn.
- DERIVED-DIRTY verdict: an external write moves server+context but not draft/snapshot, so derived isDirty still lies by
  omission - but today it lies the SAME way and then writes stale values over the server, so derived is strictly better.
  New exposure: `useUnsavedChangesGuard` becomes reachable on window close for the first time, untested. That is a real
  user-facing change and it must be in the same commit as a test, not discovered later.
- SEQUENCING RULING: does NOT jump settings-3 (its 11 boxes - backup/.ozpkg/factory reset/audit retention - touch none of the
  four shared rows, grep-verified). It DOES jump the 450 sizing queue, because the vector is live now. So D0 first, then the
  ladder resumes; and the real re-arming trigger is the `sections/` -> `screens/` migration named in agents-2 (12 of the
  `screens/` files are 32-line placeholders), which must land AFTER D0, never before.
- REJECTED, with reasons: delete page Save (provably correct today but removes the very affordance AGENTS.md uses to
  IDENTIFY the page, and forecloses the migration); rehydrate-on-markSettingsUpdated (contradicts the documented rule at
  :247-249 and eats in-flight edits). DEFERRED as the right architecture: per-key upserts - 11 individual
  `set_receipt_*` setters already exist and `setSettingScoped` is already called from this hook, so no new server code.
- Its honesty note kept: it ran no tests, so the red/green predictions for :432/:446/:498 are read off assertions. D0 must
  establish them by execution, and the `store.currency` vs `defaultCurrency` fusion at :133 is flagged unresolved - a naive
  per-field diff can report currency dirty from the other's change. That is the first thing D0 should pin with a test.

- PARKED #14 (whether the get_setting -> null mock fix ships, 'blocked by dev-mock-scoped-aliases.test.ts:81') is now ANSWERED
  by measurement: SHIP. Blast radius = 2 files / 4 cases, all of them tests that WANT to lose. Zero production files depend on
the mask.
- The mock answers `''` for EVERY key because the handler is `() => ''` with zero args and `args.key` is never read
  (handlers/settings.ts:71), while the bridge returns Ok(None) - pinned in Rust by two tests named
  get_setting_returns_none_for_missing_* (settings_tests.rs:336 + tablet twin), and the TS client already declares
  `string | null`. So the divergence is mock-vs-bridge, and there is already a characterization file whose header SAYS the
  fix must go red on purpose and delete it. Someone documented this collision instead of hiding it.

  EmailReportSettings.tsx:91, WorkspaceKdsSettings.tsx:92/93, WorkspaceInventorySettings.tsx:76,
  WorkspaceRestaurantPosSettings.tsx:78): every one maps '' and null to the same verdict. That is the double-edged fact - the
  mask costs nothing today and costs a FUTURE null branch its only preview coverage.
- THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS: mockDispatcher.ts:84-93 answers ANY `X_scoped` by calling the base handler and DISCARDING EVERY
  ARGUMENT. So in preview, get_setting_scoped('kds.density') and get_setting_scoped('anything') are the same call, and there
  are 115 such gaps. THAT is the aliasing-bug-hiding mechanism; the ''-vs-null detail is one symptom. Filed as its own item,

## Fence record for this lane (written BEFORE any write, per protocol)
- Wave N (research): read-only, no owner needed.
- Wave N+1 (test): ONE owner, ONE file - the existing lifecycle test file only (path from the dossier). The PRODUCTION hook is
  explicitly OUT of the tester's fence: if covering the branch requires changing the hook (i.e. the branch is unreachable without
  scaffolding), that is a FENCE CHANGE REQUEST and a design decision, not something a test lane does silently - re-adding a
  `pending` queue / `defer` flag to production code to feed a test is the tail wagging the dog and gets ruled on, not executed.
- Shared hot files untouched this wave: no package.json, no lockfile, no root config, no plan doc until the verdict is in.
## What settles this lane
Acceptance is a KILL PROOF, not a green test: the case must be shown to FAIL when the guard is broken (the convention the surviving
6 cases already use - three seeded defects, each killed). A case that passes with the guard deleted proves nothing and does not
close the item. Plus one whole-file vitest run and the file's own mutation restores proven by hash.

  that comment's number and forwarded it into a parked item. It was wrong by 12 sites and by one whole shell.

  (entitlements.rs:282, oz-bridge/src/subscription.rs:297, oz-api/src/routes/products.rs:279, tablet subscription.rs:288 — last one
  shape-inferred, researcher flagged it itself).
- THE SEED IS THE BUG'S SOURCE: 20260813_init.sql:1512-1514 inserts tenant_subscription(signature='BOOTSTRAP_FREE'). In release the
  #[cfg(debug_assertions)] accept at license_verification.rs:391 is gone, so :398-404 base64-decodes that literal and fails. And the
  MISSING-ROW fallback is no better: auth.rs:613-616 warns "defaulting to Free tier" then bootstrap_free() sets an EMPTY signature,
  which also fails (subscription.rs:637 -> :406-408). Both release states of an unactivated DB error.
- Client-side plan gating is UNCONDITIONAL — zero hits for enforce_plans across all four client trees. OZ_ENFORCE_PLANS is
  cloud-server-only (config.rs:161, :219-223, default OFF, .env.example ships 0). So there is no flag story that explains this away.
MY ERROR, RECORDED AGAINST ME: I told the user I would not fund the release smoke test "because a prior pass already disproved the
sentinel as a production bug, by execution". That disproof (todo-refactor-kasirmu-app-agents-3.md:144,146) disproves a CRYPTO bug —
producer/consumer alphabets agree, release really rejects the sentinel — and then writes the 39 release reds off as "100% test
fixture". The fixture IS the production seed row, and those failures are the same ?-propagation a customer would hit. I quoted the
conclusion without reading what its scope was. Withholding the smoke test on that basis was a false economy; the dossier already
contained the execution evidence (1228 pass / 76 fail at cargo test -p oz-bridge --release) that I said I needed before spending it.
STILL UNPROVEN, and it is the whole question: is create_session reachable BEFORE activation on a clean release install? If yes, an
unactivated release install cannot log in — that is a first-run outage, not a code smell. If an activation gate really holds the app
shut first, this is a latent defect. That is now the critical path, not the fix.

# PARKED #1 CLOSED WITH ITS SEVERITY CUT BY ~AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE - and it was replaced by a smaller, nastier set
87b52a05 measured the fail-open's actual reach. Headline correction to my own headline from 40 minutes ago:
THE GATE IS NOT THE BOUNDARY, SO THE FAIL-OPEN IS NOT AN ESCALATION. crates/oz-core/src/license_verification.rs:387-394 accepts the
sentinel only under #[cfg(debug_assertions)], and create_session (oz-bridge/src/auth.rs:610-619) runs validate_clock_rollback then
verify_signature? BEFORE insert_session (:632). So in release an unactivated install that slips the UI gate reaches a LOGIN SCREEN
THAT CANNOT CREATE A SESSION. The trust decision is per-command across 16+ bridge sites, all ?-propagating, i.e. fail-CLOSED at the
data layer. settings['license.payload']/['license.signature'] are read by exactly ONE function (get_license_status) and consulted by
NOTHING downstream - so those two keys gate the UI and nothing else.
WHAT THE GATE ACTUALLY COSTS, narrowed to what is real:
- The realistic openers are exactly three: (a) a global SQLite that cannot read the settings table at all (corrupt/locked/pre-
  migration) - rejects both calls; (b) a UI bundle newer than the desktop binary (command unregistered); (c) any non-Tauri context.
- NOT openers, each measured rather than assumed: a MISSING settings key (Settings::get returns Ok(None) -> status 'missing', the gate
  holds); a CONTENDED GLOBAL LOCK - ctx.rs:378-381 lock_global is infallible, so the splash HANGS forever instead of opening, which is
  its own availability bug wearing a different face; and the licence verdicts that look like errors (ClockTampered, InvalidSignature,
  Expired-past-grace, Missing) are all Ok(is_active:false), so the fresh-install gate holds correctly against every one of them.
- THE RESIDUAL EXPOSURE, and it is commercial not security: subscription.rs:652-659 - once a VALIDLY SIGNED row exists, an
  expired/revoked subscription silently reverts to Free-tier entitlements rather than denying the session. So the honest one-liner is
  'expired tenants keep working at Free tier', NOT 'anyone gets a free app'.
THREE NEW FINDINGS THE SEVERITY PASS TURNED UP:
- (a) A SECOND fail-open nobody had named: AppShell.tsx:163-165 + :416-425 - has_users is under its own nested catch, and on
  REJECTION sets hasAnyUsers=FALSE, which routes a !session install straight to CreatePinScreen. A transient DB error hands out
  OWNER-BOOTSTRAP. Steered into c91680b7's live fence (same file, same defect class - a boolean that means both 'we checked' and 'it
  is so'), with an explicit instruction to return Fence_Request/Partial rather than silently drop it.
- (b) completed=true on a never-activated install, three ways - and the interesting one is registry-shaped:
  registration_gate_debt.generated.rs:88-89 lists setup::complete_setup AND setup::dismiss_setup_wizard as no_session_resolution, i.e.
  pre-auth and callable directly over IPC, so invoke('dismiss_setup_wizard') from devtools PERMANENTLY persists the flag that
  AppShell:167-176 turns into hasActiveLicense=true. Also: setup.rs:118 writes SETUP_COMPLETE='1' which get_setup_status NEVER reads
  (write-only dead weight - the whole 'setup done' verdict rides the SHOW_SETUP_WIZARD='false' flag from a mere DISMISSAL at :181-186),
  and AppShell :437 onLaunch sets completed locally WITHOUT persisting while handleSkip :290-293 DOES persist it - two answers to the
  same question depending on which button the operator pressed.
- (c) The classification the helper decision needed is now CLOSED: inventory.rs:88-101 takes a session_token, resolves it at :95 and
  requires INVENTORY_LOCATIONS_MANAGE at :96-101 -> NOT pre-activation reachable. So the pre-activation set is 5 tablet sites
  (commands/auth.rs:441, history.rs:63, products.rs:295 'legacy pre-session command', pos.rs:784, offline.rs:162) plus bridge
  auth.rs:617 behind the UI gate. Everything else needs a token that release cannot mint without a valid signature.

devtools reachability of the setup commands rests on a verified registry fact plus an unverified UI path. Both go in the morning report

# ExpoScreen timers pinned (828247454) - three mutants, zero cross-talk, and a finding worth more than the pin
a672c078 added /11 and /12 to ui/src/__tests__/ExpoScreen.test.tsx (21 cases now), each killing EXACTLY one named case: M1 drop
clearInterval(:214) -> /11 alone; M2 drop removeEventListener(:215) -> /11 alone; M3 drop the !document.hidden gate(:203) -> /12 alone.
Neither /10 nor any of the original 19 weakens under any mutant. Restore hash-proven to dfced6630... after EVERY mutant, git restore
never used, mutation windows ~3s each - the discipline from the false-flaky incident, applied the first time it was needed.
THE FINDING: vitest fake timers return an OBJECT from setInterval whose valueOf() is the numeric id while clearInterval receives the raw
object, so created and cleared ids never match unless BOTH sides are Number()-normalized. Its first draft PASSED THE DEATH CHECK
VACUOUSLY and only found out by failing elsewhere. That is the exact shape this whole session has been hunting: an assertion that cannot
fail because the two sides it compares are different kinds of thing. Recorded in the file header, not just in its report. Also handled:
window === globalThis in jsdom means the footer's 30s clock lands in the same recording - filtered by ms === EXPO_POLL_MS and asserted
to select exactly 1. tsc reads one project-wide error in AppShell.tsx, which is 2c328022's in-flight edit, not a regression.
DISPATCHED ON THE FREED SLOT (a672c078, reused): the TABLET twin of the feature-gate pin. TabletAppShell.tsx has its own nav-only gate
(~:196) and all I have ever done is report it as untested; the desktop now has 10 pins, so the asymmetry is worth closing. Rules stated
up front because they are the ones that matter: pin CURRENT behaviour, name what is NOT covered in the header, never let a mock decide
the outcome (a test whose mock enforces the gate is theatre), and prove non-vacuity by patching the missing gate IN and showing a case
dies, restored byte-identical by hash, with the index.lock rule repeated verbatim.
STILL QUEUED AND WHY: npm run check:all cannot run while a coder is editing AppShell.tsx (it is a RUN-NOT-WRITE leg that could make two
plans renameable, so a false red from an in-flight mutation would cost more than the delay), and the -p oz-core --release twin waits for
2ff05f5c because two cargo invocations in one workspace serialize on the build-directory lock and would make each other look hung.

## Option D for the 76 (508e0f19) - the door that closed, and why (b)=0 is attribution not coverage
NO test in this crate can mint a verifying signature: verify_license_signature takes only (payload, sig) and reads the key from the
include_str! constant (license_verification.rs:44, 396, 424-430) - no key parameter, no trait, no thread-local, no injected verifier;
subscription.rs:474-477 and license.rs:594 call it directly. Only oz-license.key.pub is tracked; the private PEM is git-ignored AND ABSENT
FROM DISK. A seeded row is therefore exactly one of two kinds - sentinel (debug loads, release fails) or invalid (fails both) - and NO
THIRD KIND EXISTS without a production seam, which is an owner ruling, not a worker's fix. Every fixture inherits the sentinel anyway:
testing::temp_conn() -> migrations::fresh_db() replays 20260813_init.sql.
THE TAUTOLOGY: license_verification_tests.rs:27-64 generate a keypair and re-implement verification INLINE against the test key and never
call verify_license_signature - green in both profiles, covering nothing shipped. That is WHY the caveat can never be closed by fixtures.
RECOMMENDED D = A's per-site forks through ONE shared vocabulary (seeded_row_loads() + the fail-closed projection consts in testing.rs), a
counted and disclosed dose of C (cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), ignore="<reason naming the parked seam>")) ONLY where the release arm
would assert something unrelated to the test's purpose, plus ONE NEW #[cfg(not(debug_assertions))] test asserting the product fact - so the
release leg GAINS an assertion rather than only losing reds. Rejected by name so nobody rediscovers them: [profile.release]
debug-assertions = true (puts the licence bypass in the SHIPPED binary); signing fixtures with OZPOS_OZ_LICENSE_PRIVATE_KEY
(machine-dependent, non-CI, puts signing capability inside the test suite); blanking a signature to silence a red (loud forged-row error ->
silent Free run) - auth_tests.rs:391-409 stays Err in both profiles as the pinned counter-example. IT OVERRODE MY ORDERING: pilot a2 (11
audit cases), not a4, because a4's usize::from(cfg!(debug_assertions)) shape is unrepresentative and its fix is a predicate change, so it
discriminates nothing between A and C. Slices S1..S11 fenced BY FILE not by family; 8 serialized legs ~= 25 min, never 76 legs;
--no-fail-fast mandatory; and the ignore mechanism must be PROVEN in the pilot before 21 subscription sites depend on it.
HAND-OFF OBLIGATION I am carrying: after this work release-side SCOPE coverage is ZERO either way (the six scope tests assert fail-closed or
are ignored), so Phase 3b inherits the same invisible hole unless it is told. f8f649eb is writing the finding into
docs/records/JOURNAL.md as a dated append-only entry - explicitly NOT into todo-open-debt-program.md, which is untracked and another
session's, since committing it would publish their work under my subject.

# ROUND 28 - the review-before-fan-out paid for itself: two MAJORS on the shared contract, caught before nine lanes copied it
fedd32cf on 8229bd2b9 -> SAFE WITH ONE CAVEAT, logic sound, but two Major claims in the file's own documentation would have MISLED a copying lane:
(1) testing.rs:139-143 extends the helper to get_license_status, which is false - license.rs:594-601/685-697/659-668 has THREE different debug arms
and a different vocabulary (InvalidSignature/Missing vs Unavailable/free), and fresh_db seeds NO license.payload/signature row (0 hits in
20260813_init.sql), so the seed shapes differ in INPUTS not just outputs; (2) testing.rs:149-155 - in release, false does not mean 'the sentinel was
rejected': the else-branch collapses FIVE causes (no row, load Err, load_public_key failure, base64 reject, RSA mismatch), and the product's own
fail-closed loaders collapse them identically, so a migration that lost the seed row would go GREEN asserting fail-closed for an ABSENT row.
Plus two Minors: 'both callers reach it directly' is not a census (there are FOUR call sites - the other two are server-response verification on
activate/refresh at license_verification.rs:484,:527, and a lane that greps four against a block asserting two will conclude the proof is stale);
and the tripwire has a SILENT FLIP the doc does not name - [profile.release] debug-assertions=true compiles the sentinel arm into the SHIPPED binary
while seeded_row_loads()==cfg!(debug_assertions) stays true==true, and nothing in CI sees it because dev-ci.yml:244 is the only Rust test run and NO
--release test invocation exists in it, check.sh, release.sh or run-pre-push.py. And a Nit that matters for citations: the forged-row counter-example
is auth_tests.rs:391-430, not 391-409 - the range I quoted contains the UPDATE but not the expect_err at :428.
WHAT THE NOTES CONFIRM, which is why the helper stays: temp_conn is in-memory and deterministic (SNAPSHOT LazyLock is only the backup source, never
handed out), debug-true has NO other path, the consts match the product accessors exactly, gate polarity is genuinely right (locked<=>false because
every supports_* derives from tier and Free is false on all of them), and the module is cfg(test)-private so a cross-crate misuse is a compile error,
not a wrong green. The pre-existing poison hazard (a panic in fresh_db poisons :416 and every later temp_conn panics) was named as not-introduced.
ALSO FOUND: a debug true does NOT imply the tier projects free on desktop paths, because apply_debug_upgrade (entitlements.rs:101-109, called at
oz-bridge/src/subscription.rs:377) promotes an Active Free row to Premium - the doc guards the fail-closed side, not the live side.
ACTION TAKEN: steer sent to the PILOT (2ca3ec74) to HALT-AND-CARRY the caveat verbatim, with the concrete new requirement that every release-side arm
it writes must ALSO assert the seeded row EXISTS, the assert-not-conditional rule for FAIL_CLOSED_GATES_LOCKED, and an instruction to report honestly

acquirer or terminal field, tenant comes strictly from the JWT. SERIALISATION: serde JSON string scalar, never a URL/header/SQL, so not injection;

space in compose is Some, goes verbatim onto the wire, the gateway 400s, and EVERY QRIS charge on that deployment returns 502 - silently until the
first charge. Whitespace-only already reads None, so the guard is half-built. Second: config.rs:131 says the pin 'must stay unset in shared
multi-tenant deployments' and NOTHING enforces it, while validate_production already exists at :205/:285 but runs BEFORE the acquirer is read.
Third: no charset or length bound, whose real consequence is that a typo like "shopee" is an all-tenant outage discovered at first charge.

# ROUND 80 - pre-writing the release-fixture conversion template so the 65 can be drained by file, by lane, in parallel
The census (2bab4aa2) will hand me failures grouped by source file with a message category each. The conversion is mechanical once the shape is known, and it is the one remaining campaign on this board that is BOTH actionable tonight and invisible to CI. So the brief template is written here once, and each lane gets it with only the file name and its count changed. Six coder slots max, one FILE per lane - the files are siblings wired by #[path], so there is no shared edit surface, and two lanes in one test file would collide the way the guard file would.
THE TEMPLATE, verbatim for each lane: convert <FILE>.rs so its release-profile expectations describe the shipped release behaviour instead of the debug sentinel. Fork at RUNTIME with 'if seeded_row_loads()' from crates/oz-bridge/src/testing.rs - NEVER a #[cfg(not(debug_assertions))] arm (it does not compile when the release arm is reached by a runtime branch, and the cfg shape also breaks unused_imports under RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings in dev-ci#cargo-check). In EVERY release-side arm, first assert the seeded row EXISTS (TenantSubscription::load(...).expect(...)) before asserting what it projects, because seeded_row_loads() == false in release collapses five distinct causes and 'row absent' is one of them - that is testing.rs:183-198's rule and it is the difference between a green that means something and a green that means nothing. FAIL_CLOSED_* constants may appear ONLY as the RHS of an assert_eq!, never as an if-condition. No assertion may be deleted: the debug arm keeps its current expectations byte-for-byte, the release arm gains its own, and the commit message must state the deleted-assertion count as zero with the whitespace-insensitive diff that proves it. No #[ignore], no #[cfg_attr], no skip, no renamed-away assertion, no [profile.release] edit, no production .rs, no license seam - verify_license_signature has FOUR call sites and none of them is a fixture's to change.
PER-LANE VERIFY: cargo test -p <crate> <filter> debug AND --release, both reported with their own numbers; then the crate's full debug rollup (oz-bridge reads 1,310 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored and must not drop); cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check exit 0. Never cargo test --workspace, no clippy, no fmt --all. Expect 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory' from the other lanes in the same crate: wait it out, never delete a lock you do not own.
WHAT I MUST DO AT THE GATE, not the lanes: the count that matters is the RELEASE failure total moving 65 -> 0 across the wave, and it only means anything as ONE full 'cargo test -p oz-bridge --release --no-fail-fast' run on a quiet tree after every lane in the crate has settled. Scoped greens from six lanes are necessary and are not the gate.
IF THE CENSUS FINDS A NOT-TIER-SHAPED FAILURE, the template does not apply and that file becomes a researcher's target first: a genuine release-only product bug is a different animal from an unconverted fixture, and converting it would file the bug away. The census was asked to count those separately precisely so I do not have to guess; 283f570b named security_scoped_integration_tests.rs 'and friends', so the honest expectation is that most are fixtures and some are not.
ALSO QUEUED, unchanged: locations.rs:34 unused import and sync.rs:184 unused variable (release-only, would fail -D warnings in any release run - do them as ONE lane, and only after the crate's census lane settles so nobody's build changes under them); W3-1 four Cards; W3-3 Memos; W3-4 PaymentModal after 7f8c0ef9's cascade verdict; importWizard hook after exportWizard lands; and the customer-badge extraction, which now has b024da46e's 598-line suite in front of it.

# ROUND 200 - the object store ate a commit, and the session's first repo-integrity repair
At 04:55 I ran git log for a routine status check and got fatal: bad object HEAD. git rev-parse still printed 7567d7ce8, git cat-file said it was not a valid object, and git fsck named it as an invalid sha1 pointer for both HEAD and refs/heads/0.0.39, plus an invalid sha1 pointer in the index cache-tree and TWO missing blobs. The branch tip pointed at a commit that did not exist. Nothing in git log, git status or git commit worked, which meant every lane in flight would fail at its commit step and the whole session was about to stall blind.
THE CAUSE, from the store's own timestamps rather than a guess: .git/objects/info carried a commit-graph chain and a fresh graph file stamped 04:54, a multi-pack-index stamped 04:53, a 2.1 MB pack stamped 04:53, and objects/info/packs named a pack file that is not on disk. The commit was written at 04:53:53. The strong reading is a gc, repack or prune racing the write and treating the new objects as unreachable before the ref settled - which also explains why the object count went to zero loose dirs and why the blobs vanished with it. Something ran maintenance in this checkout that none of my lanes was told about.
WHAT I DID, in this order: back up the branch tip, the whole reflog and the index into .agents/git-repair-2026-09-15/, inside the directory my journal already lives in and is gitignored, so the repair leaves no staged bytes and no tracked change; then git update-ref refs/heads/0.0.39 c52a9a1af, the newest commit that still resolves. No commit before that was touched, no working tree was modified, and the three operations I will not use on a shared checkout - reset --hard, checkout, stash - were not used, because each one would have deleted in-flight edits from six lanes.
WHAT THE REPAIR COST AND SAVED: exactly one commit was at risk, 7567d7ce8, the AGENTS.md stylesheet-law re-land, and its CONTENT SURVIVED because a lost object does not delete a working tree - grep found the new paragraph in both mirrors on disk, and git status showed both files staged against the repaired tip. So the recovery was a re-commit rather than a rewrite, and 5272e648 landed it as 32886394e with the reachability check I should have been running all night: git cat-file -t on the commit's own SHA, and git merge-base --is-ancestor against HEAD. It reported the distinction better than I would have - the commit passed every gate that saw it and was simply not retained - which is the strongest possible support for the paragraph in the mirror that a lane cannot read its own commit's silence as proof of anything.
TWO LANES SAW THE SAME THING AND NEITHER MADE IT WORSE. 95c6d8f4 diagnosed it from the object-store timestamps independently, found the lost commit's content intact on disk, and REFUSED to move a shared tip under live lanes because reset is the recovery the repo's own §3 withdrew - it asked for the owner's authority instead of improvising. e564f544 hit could not resolve HEAD on its commit, wrote all thirteen dispositions to disk anyway, reported the fsck output verbatim, and stopped without attempting a repair. And the same lane is the one that told me not to trust its own green: verify-agents-mirrors reads HEAD: in seventeen places, so while HEAD was unreadable the mirror checker was grading nothing and still exiting 0. I have asked for both gates to be re-run against a readable HEAD, because the false-clean window is three minutes wide and every gate that printed during it is unverified.
STATE OF THE STORE NOW: fsck reports zero missing blobs; what remains is four invalid reflog entries naming the pruned SHA, which is a scar and not a fault, plus ordinary dangling trees. I left the reflog alone - expiring entries is a write into the store, and I want exactly one hand in it while maintenance may still be running. Three commits landed after the repair: the locations fixtures at 18e368558, another session's topology review at 2ed08331e, and the mirror re-land at 32886394e, which is HEAD.
THE CAMPAIGN CROSSES A LINE: locations landed, so the release reds are 28 measured at e008ade98 minus 13 auth minus 2 locations = 13, and the MEASURED crate release triple at 18e368558 is 1,296 passed and 13 failed in 181 seconds. My derived 1,294/15 was two off on both sides because a derivation holds the pass count still while other lanes are adding tests - which is a general lesson I have now paid for twice tonight. The remainder is staff 4, auth::security_integration_tests 4, terminals 2, staff::security_events 2, and one deliberate red I am not going to fix, the auth case asserting a written-audit-row count parametrised on cfg!(debug_assertions), where release measures 1 and the name claims 0. Whether a production Free tenant should record that row is a product ruling and it is parked.
TWO SHAPES THE FIXTURE LANES FOUND THAT MY TEMPLATE DID NOT WARN ABOUT, both now in the next brief by name: a release red is not always an unwrap on a propagated Err - twice it was the fixture's OWN sub_kind assertion, because the signature check pre-empts the gate the test was written to exercise, so the fixture names the wrong winner - and a tier stamp can assert the wrong TABLE, because locations re-tiers through the store db while the existence pin reads the global identity row, and only the assert caught it. That is the second time a lane has had to correct the shape of my mechanical rule rather than just its numbers.
AND THE RETIREMENT THAT GOT HONESTER AS IT GOT CLOSER: the weight-scale widget is a true orphan - zero importers across three greps including the unfiltered one, no e2e selector, and the lazy-registration indirection checked - but deleting it is now a SEVEN-path commit, because it pairs with BASELINE_UNCITED's line at :1556, the native-tooltip ratchet's entry at scripts/native-tooltip-baseline.json:20, the component's own 188-line test dying with 12 cases, and SIXTEEN Fluent keys in sales.ftl and its id twin that the widget is the only consumer of. The last of those is the important one: hook step 7 exists to stop a deleted reference stranding a key, it is --staged-only, and a component deletion stages no bundle, so the one gate whose rule covers this case cannot see it unless the deletion stages the bundles deliberately. I have fenced the whole set to one lane for exactly that reason.
METRICS after 200 rounds: 44 commits by my lanes tonight, one repo-integrity repair, zero interrupts, zero breaker trips, zero red wave gates until the store itself went red underneath all of them - and the recovery took a backup, one update-ref, and a lane that had the sense not to touch a shared tip it did not own.

The lane that hit the corruption also answered my false-clean question properly rather than taking comfort: verify-agents-mirrors prints the same verdict before and after, but with a readable HEAD it now prints the per-file HEAD: legs it printed nothing for an hour ago, so the earlier green was luck and not evidence. Same output, different standing. That is the whole lesson of the night in one line - a gate that cannot read its input exits 0 exactly like a gate whose input is clean.
THE GUARD IS 1,747 LINES, UP FROM 1,368 WHEN I STARTED READING IT TONIGHT, and its last commit is the widget retirement. Three separate lanes have now told me the census they handed me is an hour stale against their own work, which is correct and is why every brief says re-derive. The utils file that actually decides what counts as used has not changed since 209a6fd7e on 2026-09-05 - 199 lines, byte-current against every read I made tonight - so the semantics are stable even while the runner's line numbers are not.
THE SCOPING QUESTION, ANSWERED PROPERLY AND ANSWERED NO: widening additionalTsx registers nothing tonight. Case 3 must be empty to land a citation because soft is soft in name only, and the three rows measured under BOTH scopings still read 39, 38 and 5 dead names under feature-directory scoping - RetailPosScreen, NodeTopologyEditor, AnalyticsScreen. A hundred-fold reduction is still non-zero, and non-zero is red. So the unlock count from a scope change is zero and what it actually buys is an honest deletion list, 39 to remove instead of 301.
THE POLARITY POINT, which is the reason I will not treat this knob as a mute: additionalTsx feeds all three cases and in the case-1 direction it ADDS obligations, because every newly-listed file's class names must now be defined somewhere the entry can see. A mute removes a name from case 1, the one check that catches markup naming nothing; this removes findings from case 3 while tightening case 1. Different sign, different law, and the asymmetry is brutal in the right way - a wrong path crashes collection with an ENOENT during the describe.each body, so an over-broad path is the only one that can pass silently. Five or more entries already carry multi-file lists, so the shape is house style, but every one of them is provenance-scoped - code that moved out of THIS screen - and the header at :77-81 ships the falsification test for each line. A sibling that merely shares a sheet is not what any existing list claims.
THE REAL DEFECT THAT CAME OUT OF THE ANALYSIS, and it is the file's own: used is a Set of names, not of (name, file) pairs, so on a shared sheet the guard cannot tell who consumes what. Since 2026-09-05 the repo has moved to many-owners-per-sheet and the guard still presumes one owner per sheet, which means the honest fix is a third axis whose used set is a readdir-derived family - the coverage case already does exactly that walk - and not a lane-written list of 13 to 53 paths. That goes to the owner page as the shape of the decision, not into my backlog as a slice.
WHAT I AM FUNDING INSTEAD: the 37 case-1 names, because they are the only finding in the census that is a fact about CSS rather than a fact about the guard's used set, and unlike case 3 they cannot be argued away by changing scope. The sequencing insight is the overlap - a name defined for case 1 stops being a deletion candidate for case 3, so one pass per sheet settles both columns and two queues would double the work. I have asked for the three-way disposition of each name, because define, delete-from-markup and reclassify-as-external are three different jobs with three different risk profiles and one of them is a render change in a .tsx. A lane that treats all 37 as one work type will guess, and guessing on an unmounted sheet is how you delete a class a Playwright locator needs.
LANDED SINCE THE LAST JOURNAL: 18e368558 locations fixtures, 08b11846e the thirteen payment closures, 338c15c01 the weight-scale retirement as a seven-path commit carrying two baseline shrinks and sixteen Fluent keys, 6049844dc the KDS ticks and owner-page item 8, plus 32886394e the mirror re-land. 46 commits by my lanes tonight. The widget box is the one I would point a new reader at: an orphan three greps confirmed, paired with the guard line, the tooltip ratchet entry, its own 12-case suite and the keys it strands - and the reason it took seven paths is that the hook step written to stop a deleted reference stranding a key is --staged-only and cannot see a deletion that stages no bundle.

# ROUND 202 - three lanes measured my brief wrong and were right, and the campaign is at 11
Four settles, and the pattern is now unmistakable: the lanes that read the code before obeying me are producing better commits than the ones that did not.
THE TOOLTIP BOX, a43314d65. I briefed a component swap - native title to shared Tooltip - and the lane found the instruction wrong in every half and landed a one-line deletion instead. Tooltip returns a div.tooltip-wrapper around its child at :224, which on an icon-only button in a flex row is a cashier-header layout change bought for nothing, and at :233 it supplies only aria-describedby and only while shown, so it never provides an accessible name at all. The title it deleted was a duplicate of the aria-label two lines above, using the same Fluent key. THEN THE FINDING THAT MAKES IT AN OWNER ITEM AND NOT A WIN: re-running the compliance test's own AST rule over 377 non-test .tsx files reads 43 elements carrying a native title beside an aria-label, 29 of them passing the IDENTICAL expression to both, spread over six features. So the duplicate is the common shape and not a defect class, and the generalisation of my box would have bought forty-three wrapper divs. And the ratchet's total field is read by no code path - the test recomputes it by summing per-file counts - so it had already drifted out of agreement with its own data, reading 79 when the true sum was 76 after the widget retirement, and the JSON's own carry_forward_note was instructing the next reader to do the Tooltip conversion that just measured wrong.
THE FALLBACK GATE, 70acd1b34, +258 lines, 17 to 20 cases, and it went 258 insertions with zero deletions because it adds a law rather than replacing one. The rule: a var() with a literal tail is a hard refusal unless the token is declared in :root or in both theme blocks, and additionally frozen at today's population unless its declarations agree byte-for-byte across the blocks it appears in. It found zero live tails today - light-not-root is 0 names and dark-not-root-or-light is 0 - and a much larger grandfathered population, 98 name-at-sheet pairs over 156 sites where the declarations DISAGREE. The lane's own sequencing advice is the good part: sweep the 46 now, hold the 106 root-only tails until the law has been red on somebody, because a sweep that outruns its own gate is how ef6b4d5bf became a subset of its own premise. Its honesty note too: it could not plant a violation in /tmp because vitest will not collect outside its root, so it proved teeth with three in-file mutations and restored each, verified byte-identical afterward.
THE RED CENSUS, read-only, and it corrected three of my beliefs at once. My module name was wrong - the four remaining auth integration reds live in auth::security_scoped_integration_tests via auth.rs:1349's #[path] wiring, not the name I have been typing, and the similarly-named security_scoped is a different module this campaign never touched. And the classification of the remaining thirteen, by two independent methods that agree - scoreboard arithmetic against the JOURNAL's 65-to-44 census, and gate-mapping from the nine verify_signature()? call sites onto the tests that reach them: PROPAGATION 9, EXPECTED-CAUSE MISMATCH 1, PROJECTION or VACUITY 2, PROFILE-HYBRID 1. The two security_events cases are the NO TEMPLATE I had been told about and could not explain: one is mechanically forkable but its assertion that a row count is 1 would become false evidence, and the other's entire claim - a rejected create records no security event - would be satisfied for the WRONG REASON once release rejects at the signature gate instead of the duplicate. THE NAME PROGRAMME, and it shrank the way the good ones do. # ROUND 203 - two refusals, one non-contradiction, and the mute census
TWO LANES REFUSED MY BRIEF TONIGHT AND BOTH WERE RIGHT, which is the single best metric I have. 5272e648 was told to extract the front half of the EDC flow onto a duplication premise I inherited: it hashed all 182 shell windows against all 66 hook windows and found ZERO identical bodies, then pointed at useEdcTenderPhase.ts:17-20 where the boundary decision is WRITTEN DOWN - the gateway helpers exist once and are passed DOWN, because owning them in one tender's hook would make that hook own three tenders' completion. The premise was not stale, it was invented. It also refused my VERIFY clause rather than faking it: useTenderState.ts and usePaymentFlow do not exist in that directory, and PaymentModal.test.tsx prints 27 cases, not the 51 I quoted. The box is closed with a rule attached: never brief a hoist without a hash of the two bodies.
It did leave the owner page richer than it found it, and this is the best citation set anyone has produced on the payment shell: three settle-shaped tails that disagree ON PURPOSE - settleGatewaySale reads back at :651-653 before finalizing at :691, void gated by a parameter, toasts through l10nRef.current, with an ADR #7 comment explaining that an ambient read from the wrong store once showed a customer the wrong total; the direct path finalizes at :945 BEFORE reading back at :964, void unconditional, closes over the render value at :1004. A terminal holds captured money and cash does not. My 'two codepaths' was an understatement and a parameterised seam would have been a lie.
3c026b27 was told to delete two empty rules in KdsScreen.css and took outcome three - land nothing - for a reason I had not thought of: a Playwright locator resolves against the DOM class attribute, not the stylesheet, so removing a brace pair cannot un-class a div. The deletion was SAFE and WORTHLESS, and it said so. It also confirmed the empties at :1807 and :1808 by two scanning methods after the analyst's regex missed both by forbidding whitespace inside the braces, counted the bare-name consumers - .kds-columns at nine locator sites across three specs, .kds-column under a toHaveCount(3) at kds.spec.ts:65 - and answered my follow-up: the two empties and the three variant-less names are ONE decision, all five are pure selector anchors and none styles anything.
THE PARENTCSS 'CONTRADICTION' WAS MINE AND ONLY MINE. The researcher went to the file and the history and found: 99c98427f never touched the guard - git show returns an empty diff for it - and the narrowing was 132f08866 at 03:09, +129/-8. The rule has TWO legal shapes and names settings/SettingsPage.css as the example of the first one, so the four settings cites are the rule's own illustration, not violations of it. My paraphrase - 'may name only ../frontend/themes/' - collapsed a shape out of existence and I nearly cancelled a funded programme on it. That is the same error class I have been logging all night, and this time the source was my own summary of a law rather than a stale number.
AND THE RULE IS REAL, THREE HARD CHECKS: the escaping-prefix law at :1605-1613, parent-sheet existence at :1660, and non-vacuity plus backing at :1682-1700, which requires that every leaner the entry uses is actually defined in the cited parent AND that there is at least one. Three lanes have already had trial theme-sheet cites REFUSED RED as vacuous at :1217, :1233 and :1264-1265 and shipped with no exemption. A cite cannot be decorative on this file. # ROUND 209 - my grep was wrong because of my own tool layer, and the font plan is one decision
The lanes were right three times and I was wrong once, in a way that generalises. My command was a line-anchored open-box grep with backslash-escaped brackets, and it printed 0 on three files that hold 5, 2 and 4 open boxes. The cause is not regex and not the files: the backslashes do not survive the JSON layer on the way into bash, so the pattern arrived as a CHARACTER CLASS MATCHING A SPACE and cannot match a literal hyphen-space-bracket. Re-run with the bracket-class form every lane has been using and the counts come out 5, 2 and 4, exactly what they reported.
What that costs me to know: every count I have quoted that came out of my own run_code with escaped brackets is suspect, and the ones from lanes are not, because they ran real shell - payment's 38 to 30, KDS's 15 to 10, pos-3's 12 to 11 all agree with their files. The fix is a canonical command I can paste without escaping anything, asked for as a deliverable with three plans as proof, together with a check of whether any plan's stated total can be reproduced by the counting command printed beside it. A documented command that does not run is worse than none - a line one of these lanes wrote about itself, and now true of my briefing layer too.
THE FONT PLAN, which I had briefed as box-less and which is a real five-open-box list: its verdict is one owner decision and no tasks. Four of the five rows are consequences of a single unbundled-fonts ruling and one is a not-a-task that asks that nothing change - and the not-a-task is genuinely reassuring, because it re-proved that the 126 deleted fallback tails and the 93 root-only tails never touched the font stacks, whose declarations are byte-identical back to 6a32cc9dd. That is the pair of batches this session should be proudest of: both proved inert, and the plan that worried about a third surface checked that it had not been touched.
AND THE GAP THAT PLAN EXPOSES is the opposite kind of debt, which is why it is an owner item and not a queue: --leading-tight EXISTS at tokens.css:170 as 1.25, with --leading-normal 1.5 and --leading-relaxed 1.625, and the tree uses var(--leading-*) 45 times against 218 LITERAL line-height declarations across 70 stylesheets. Tokenising those 218 is a RENDERING change, not an inertness-preserving cleanup - the retail tile box proved the mismatch is real by keeping line-height 1.2 rather than adopting a token that exists at a different value, and it refused the token because the VALUE disagreed, not because the token was missing.
Both of tonight's CSS batches were proved unable to render. These 218 are proved to be rendering right now. That is the sentence the owner page needs, because a lane that has only read tonight's commits could reasonably conclude that literal-versus-token mismatch is always deletable debt and start a sweep that moves type. Ask whether the leading scale is a target the UI normalises onto, which means deciding values first and reviewing a layout change, or whether literals stay legal off-scale and the 45 token uses are the exception. And measure how many of the 218 already sit at a token's value, because that minority is a cite-only sweep with no layout risk and the question only bites on the rest.

## Rules earned this round
- Manager-side counting must use bracket-class forms like [[:space:]] and never backslash-escaped literals: the escapes do not survive the JSON-to-bash layer and silently produce a char class matching a space.
- SHA existence check: git cat-file -t, never -e with a caret-brace suffix, because cmd.exe eats the caret and reports everything missing.
- Literal-versus-token mismatch is only inert debt when the literal provably cannot render. A line-height that renders is a layout change waiting to be reviewed, not a sweep.
- Pathspec commits must be built from the lane's own edit map and never from git status --porcelain, which is how 42e6c8201 swept two other sessions' sheets.
